THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER 1.
Heard Smt.Nagaratna Y.Naik, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Praveena Y.Devareddiyavara, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent No.1/ State.
2. It is the case of the prosecution that the father of the victim has lodged a complaint stating that on 03.04.2023 his daughter went along with his dog for walking at about 7.30 a.m.
However, even after lapse of 1 O'clock, she did not return to the home.
Thereafter, the complainant started searching the whereabouts of his daughter.
As he did not get her whereabouts, he has lodged a complaint before the respondent/police.
The respondent/police have registered a case in Crime No.59/2023 for the offence u/sec.363 of IPC and started investigation.
During investigation, the facts have been unfolded that the petitioner is a relative of the complainant and uncle of the victim.
On 03.04.2023, the petitioner called the victim and asked her to sit in the car and took her to Attanige village and thereafter, both were staying near dam.
The petitioner took her to Kumata and stayed there in the room of his friend and sexually assaulted the victim.
Thereafter, the victim was secured by the jurisdictional police and produced her before the Magistrate to record her statement as per Section 164 of Cr.P.C. on 25.04.2023 her statement was recorded.
The jurisdictional police after conducting the investigation, submitted the charge sheet.

4. It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is innocent of the alleged offence and he has not committed any offence as stated either in the complaint or in the statement of the victim.
5. It is further submitted that the petitioner is the uncle of the victim, on 03.04.2023, the victim had her mathematics examination.
The victim was afraiding of the examination and requested the petitioner to help her in taking her to some other place as she did not intend to attend the exam.
The petitioner in order to ease her burden, NC: 2023:KHC-D:13298 took her to his house and later, he took her to some places.
In the meantime, the complainant had lodged a complaint regarding missing of his daughter.

Therefore, the police have secured the victim and arrested the petitioner on Fakirswamy Alias Vinay S/O. Shankrappa ... vs The State Of Karnataka on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54400954/
2 12.04.2023.
6.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the petitioner is the permanent resident of Attanige village, Mundgod Taluk.
He is the earning member of the family.
He will abide the conditions imposed by this Court in the event of his release on bail.
Making such submission, learned counsel for the petitioner prays to allow the petition.

7. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader vehemently opposed the bail petition and submitted that the alleged offence is heinous in nature, the petitioner has committed sexual assault on the minor.
The petitioner being uncle of the victim has committed the offence.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for bail.
Making such submission, learned High Court Government Pleader prays to reject the bail petition.

Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the averments of the charge sheet and the complaint, the petitioner is said to have induced the victim, who is aged about 16 years and 4 months and he has abducted her from her lawful custody of her parents and committed sexual assault.
The statement recorded under Section 164 of Code of Criminal Procedure which clearly indicates that the petitioner has committed sexual assault.

Considering the gravity,
nature of the offences and also impact on the society of such crime, it is appropriate to reject the bail.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The criminal petition stands dismissed.
